note: Jayden Daniels triumphantly returned to the huddle last week as the QB2 for the week. That was on the strength of nine rushing attempts, 103 rushing yards, and two rushing scores. I don't think we can count on a hundo on the ground weekly from Daniels, but it was nice to see him running despite the brace. Daniels hasn't been good as a passer this season. Among 30 qualifying passers, Daniels has the fifth-fewest yards per attempt, the ninth-lowest passing success rate, the fourth-lowest catchable target rate, and the third-lowest hero throw rate. He'll have to get a ton of his fantasy production from his legs again this week against the 49ers. The 49ers pass defense has been a shutdown unit this season, allowing the third-fewest yards per attempt, the eighth-lowest passing success rate, and the seventh-lowest CPOE. Daniels could easily be a QB1 again this week with his rushing production alone, but also Washington will be forced to attempt to keep pace with the 49ers' high-powered offense.

I'm expecting Caleb Williams to return this week (hamstring). He opened this week with a full practice. In his only full game this season, Williams was the QB1 for the week with 37.3 fantasy points. He completed 72.4% of his passes with 9.3 yards per attempt, two passing scores, ten rushing attempts, and 65 yards on the ground (two rushing scores). I'm expecting some muted rushing production from Williams in his first game back from a hamstring injury, but I easily could be wrong there. In Week 1, Williams has a solid 7.85 aDOT and 76.4% catchable target rate. We'll see how Williams shakes off the rust against a surprising Atlanta pass defense. The Falcons have allowed the sixth-fewest yards per attempt, the seventh-lowest passing success rate, and the 13th-lowest CPOE. Williams can still return QB1 production in a tough matchup with Ben Johnson at the controls.

After a miserable 1.8 fantasy points last week, Tyler Shough has dipped to the QB15 in fantasy points per game. Shough was under duress on 46.2% of his dropbacks last week as Brian Flores had him in a blender. This week, Shough could have a solid bounce-back game. Among 29 qualifying passers, Shough is 17th in passing success rate and 20th in highly accurate throw rate, but he is also tenth in catchable target rate and sixth in hero throw rate. The Saints offense rides on his arm weekly. They don't have the ability to run the ball, so it is all on Shough to move this offense. Shough should have more time in the pocket this week and have more success. The Giants have the fifth-lowest pressure rate while giving up the 14th-highest passing success rate, the 13th-highest CPOE, and the 12th-most EPA per dropback.

Bryce Young is the QB3 in fantasy points per game. He has been excellent this season. Young has at least 21.5 fantasy points in four of his five games this season. Among 29 qualifying passers, Young is seventh in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, 21st in highly accurate throw rate, and eighth in hero throw rate. He should see enough volume to finish as a QB1 again this week. Philly has been all over the map in defensive stats, ranking 18th in yards per attempt while giving up the ninth-highest EPA per dropback and allowing the 15th-lowest CPOE. This is best viewed as a neutral matchup for Young.

Despite last week's down game, Kirko Chainz is the QB11 in fantasy points per game. Among 29 qualifying passers, he is 12th in yards per attempt, 11th in passing success rate, 15th in highly accurate throw rate, and 17th in catchable target rate. The King of Kohl's could bounce back this week with another QB1 performance. The Bills' pass defense hasn't been an imposing unit. They have allowed the second-most passing yards, the 12th-most yards per attempt, and the fifth-highest EPA per dropback and passing success rate.

C.J. Stroud is the QB16 in fantasy points per game after QB5 and QB9 finishes in the last two weeks in weekly scoring. Stroud has been balling. I will not say that he is back to his rookie season form because he looks even better than that. Among 29 qualifying passers, Stroud is 11th in yards per attempt, eighth in passing success rate, fourth in highly accurate throw rate, third in hero throw rate, and he has the second-highest aDOT. All of those metrics are incredibly impressive, especially when you consider his high aDOT. Stroud might come back to Earth some this week, but it's also possible that he excels. The Jags have been a bend but don't break defense that pressures the quarterback well (seventh in pressure rate). Jacksonville has allowed the seventh-highest yards per attempt while ranking 17th in passing success rate and 19th in CPOE. They have given up the second-fewest passing touchdowns. Stroud could be a QB1 this week if he can navigate their pass rush, but I'm not expecting a smash performance.

YOLO Jameis is back, baby! Over the last two weeks, Jameis Winston has been the QB8 and QB6 in weekly fantasy scoring. Since Week 4, among 28 qualifying quarterbacks, Winston has the eighth-most passing yards, the 11th-highest passer rating, the fifth-highest aDOT (10.1), the sixth-highest fantasy points per dropback, and is ranked 18th in catchable target rate. Winston should flirt with QB1 production again this week. The Saints have allowed the tenth-most yards per attempt, the fourth-highest passing success rate, the third-highest CPOE, and the 11th-most fantasy points per dropback.

Jacoby Brissett is the QB18 in fantasy points per game with two QB1 outings in weekly scoring (QB4, QB7). Brissett continues to operate as a low-aDOT point guard for Arizona. Among 29 qualifying passers, Brissett has the lowest yards per attempt, the tenth-lowest passer rating, the ninth-lowest aDOT, and the 12th-lowest deep passing rate. Brissett is headed toward another middling QB2 performance this week. The Rams have held passers to the second-fewest yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest passer rating, the second-lowest passing success rate, and the 12th-lowest EPA per dropback.

Deshaun Watson is the QB21 in fantasy points per game. Watson remains an overrated point guard who is still struggling with accuracy. Among 29 qualifying passers, Watson has the 13th-fewest yards per attempt, the sixth-lowest aDOT, and the fifth-highest turnover-worthy throw rate. Watson also ranks 15th in passing success rate while having the fifth-highest rate of passing yards arising from yards after the catch. Watson helped his fantasy value by adding 7.4 rushing attempts and 33.4 rushing yards per game. Watson is a passable QB2 again this week. Baltimore is 15th in passing success rate and EPA per dropback allowed while holding passers to the 14th-fewest yards per attempt.

After two weeks of fun as Jameis Rodgers, Ole Aaron turned back into a low aDOT machine last week. Against Indy last week, Rodgers had a 4.29 aDOT with only a 3.2% deep ball rate. We'll see which version we get of Rodgers this week, but that was disappointing to see. Rodgers still had a nice fantasy day as the QB11 for the week. Rodgers has had at least 22 fantasy points in each of his last three games, as he has been the QB4 in fantasy points per game since Week 3. How successful the Bucs' blitz plan is this week will go a long way to determining how Rodgers plays. The Bucs have allowed the 14th-most passing yards while ranking 15th in CPOE and 16th in EPA per dropback. The Bucs continue to blitz, though, despite it not helping their pressure rate. Tampa Bay has the fourth-highest blitz rate, but they also have the lowest pressure rate in the NFL. Against the blitz, Rodgers has the sixth-fewest yards per attempt and the fifth-lowest passing success rate. Rodgers could be a QB1 this week again, or he could fall flat. There's a wide range of outcomes for the cave dweller this week.

Daniel Jones has been a disaster this season as the QB33 in fantasy points per game. Among 37 qualifying passers, Jones has the third-fewest yards per attempt, the fourth-lowest passer rating, the tenth-lowest passing success rate, and the third-lowest CPOE. Jones has ZERO mobility in the pocket or outside of it. Jones has not surpassed ten rushing yards in any game this season. Yes, I know that's not surprising after the Achilles injury last year, but it's worth noting. Jones flubbed a nice matchup against the Commanders recently, so while he could take advantage of a porous Tennessee secondary, I'm not overly optimistic that he will. The Titans have allowed the sixth-most yards per attempt, the fifth-highest passing success rate, and the second-highest CPOE.

After taking a shot to the ribs late in the game last week, it sounds like Michael Penix will play this week. He opened the week with a full practice. Penix is the QB23 in fantasy points per game. Among 31 qualifying passers, he is second in yards per attempt, sixth in passing success rate, and 19th in catchable target rate. Atlanta hasn't asked a lot of him, as he has the second-highest rate of throwing to his first read while also having the ninth-lowest aDOT. Good thing for Penix is the Chicago pass defense isn't very good. The Bears have allowed the second-most yards per attempt, the 11th-highest passer rating, and the eighth-most fantasy points per dropback this season.

Jalon Daniels has been a decent QB2 over the last two weeks as the QB21 and QB19 in weekly scoring. He has helped his weekly floor with 7.5 rushing attempts and 39 rushing yards per game. He has facilitated a conservative passing game from the Bucs in these two starts. In those two games, he hasn't exceeded 200 passing yards or 27 passing attempts. The Bucs haven't asked a ton of the rookie. Among 34 qualifying quarterbacks, Daniels is 20th in passing success rate, 33rd in aDOT, 26th in CPOE, and seventh in catchable target rate. He has the sixth-highest first-read rate and the highest rate of passing yardage coming from yards after the catch (74.5%). The Bucs plan with him has been to get the ball out to his playmakers and hit his first reads. Daniels should be able to post solid QB2 numbers again this week against a Pittsburgh pass defense that has allowed the 11th-most yards per attempt, the eighth-highest passing success rate, and the 14th-highest EPA per dropback.

Sam Darnold is the QB24 in fantasy points per game with only one game above QB17 in weekly scoring. He has failed to clear 200 passing yards in two of his three starts this season. Among 29 qualifying passers, his numbers don't look great as he is ninth in yards per attempt, but he is also 12th-lowest in passing success rate, fourth-lowest in aDOT, and he has the fifth-lowest hero throw rate. His per-dropback accuracy metrics are sound, but I chalk that up to the low aDOT assisting him in those realms. Denver has had their defensive issues this season, but their pass defense has remained quite good. I don't see a breakout or bounce-back game for Darnold this week. Denver has held passers to the tenth-fewest yards per attempt, the eighth-lowest CPOE, and the fourth-fewest EPA per dropback.

Bo Nix is having a miserable season. He looks even worse than the rookie-season version of himself. Nix is the QB29 in fantasy points per game with only one game above QB18 in weekly scoring. Among 29 qualifying passers, Nix has the fourth-lowest yards per attempt and passing success rate, the lowest aDOT, the sixth-lowest catchable target rate, and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per dropback. Nix having the lowest aDOT and still having a catchable target rate that low is absolutely crazy work. It's wild that he can be THAT inaccurate. Geez. Shocking, but I don't see Nix bouncing back this week. Seattle remains a suffocating defense against the pass, allowing the fewest yards per attempt, the third-lowest passing success rate, and the second-fewest EPA per dropback. Sit Nix.

Justin Herbert is having a nightmare fuel season as the QB33 in fantasy points per game. Herbert is lacking pass catchers, a run game, and an offensive line. Ya know...just everything a quarterback needs to succeed in the NFL. No worries. Among 29 qualifying passers, Herbert has the tenth-fewest yards per attempt, the sixth-lowest passing success rate, the third-highest turnover-worthy throw rate, and the fifth-fewest fantasy points per dropback. This week doesn't look any better facing a Kansas City pass defense that has limited passers to the fifth-fewest yards per attempt, the third-lowest CPOE, and the third-fewest fantasy points per dropback. Sit Herbert until further notice.

Cam Ward has looked lost this season as the QB30 in fantasy points per game. Among 37 qualifying passers, Ward has the second-fewest yards per attempt, the eighth-lowest passing success rate, the lowest highly accurate throw rate, and the second-lowest hero throw rate. Ward hasn't thrown for multiple passing touchdowns this season, and he also hasn't had more than 225 passing yards in any game. The Colts have not fielded a good pass defense this season, but I have zero faith that Ward will be able to take advantage of the nice matchup. Indy has allowed the fourth-most yards per attempt, the seventh-highest passer rating, and the tenth-most EPA per dropback.

Geno Smith is the QB24 in fantasy points per game, and that's really only on the strength of his game against the Lions. In his four other starts this season, Smith has failed to surpass 250 passing yards or toss for multiple scores in any of them. Among 29 passers, Smith is 13th in yards per attempt, 15th in passing success rate, 12th in hero throw rate, and he has the third-lowest aDOT. Smith is likely turning in another middling QB2 performance this week. New England has held passers to the 13th-fewest yards per attempt, the 11th-lowest CPOE, the seventh-fewest EPA per dropback, and the ninth-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

With TreVeyon Henderson sidelined, Rhamondre Stevenson will be the Pats workhorse back. Last week, in the final two quarters of the game without Henderson, Stevenson had a 67.6% snap rate, four of the nine running back rushing attempts, and a 55% route share (10.5% target share). Considering the Pats blew out the Raiders last week, it likely impacted Stevenson's usage on early downs. Stevenson has been an efficient player on a per-touch basis which is consistent with his career marks. Among 42 qualifying rushers this season, Stevenson is 18th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Stevenson should rip the Jets run defense apart this week. New York has allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-most yards before contact per attempt, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

After his monster game last week, Bucky Irving is the RB14 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.4 touches and 95.4 total yards. Among 42 qualifying rushers, Irving is 26th in yards after contact per attempt and 18th in missed tackle rate. Irving will have a tougher matchup this week, but he can still return RB2 value. Pittsburgh has the 14th-lowest explosive run rate, the ninth-lowest rushing success rate, and the sixth-highest stuff rate.

Braelon Allen likely draws another start this week for the injured Breece Hall. Over the last two weeks, Allen has finished as the RB33 and RB8 in weekly scoring, averaging 20.5 touches and 91.5 total yards while playing 88.2% of the snaps. Allen has been New York's bell cow. Among 42 qualifying backs, Allen is 11th in yards after contact per attempt and 14th in missed tackle rate. Allen should have another nice stat line this week against a Patriots run defense that has allowed the 11th-highest rushing success rate, the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt, and has the 12th-lowest rate of hitting backs at or behind the line of scrimmage.

Cam Skattebo is the RB23 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.2 touches and 74.6 total yards. He has 11 of the team's 20 running back red zone rushing attempts. Najee Harris has cut into his workload in that region of the field with seven attempts. Among 42 qualifying backs, Skattebo is 17th in yards after contact per attempt and 22nd in missed tackle rate. Skattebo should find more running room this week against a Saints' run defense that has allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the second-highest rushing success rate, and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate. Skattebo remains a volume-based RB2.

Over the last two games, Emanuel Wilson has been Seattle's clear workhorse back. He has averaged 23 touches and 96 total yards with RB6 and RB20 weekly finishes. In those two games, he has averaged 60.2% of the snaps with 69.5% of the rushing attempts, a 36.1% route share, and an 11.8% target share. Among 42 qualifying backs, Wilson is 24th in yards after contact per attempt and 33rd in missed tackle rate. Wilson should have another productive day in Week 6. Denver has allowed the sixth-highest explosive run rate, the most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

Bhayshul Tuten continues to earn more of the Jags' backfield weekly while rocking along as the RB19 in fantasy points per game. I discussed Tuten's horrible touchdown luck last week in the Primer. This week, he saw a ton of volume, but was unable to get into the endzone or break a big run, despite being close many times. Last week, Tuten saw season-highs in snap rate (66.2%), designed carry share (91.7%), and route share (43.2%). Tuten has seen his numbers in all three categories climb weekly. Among 42 qualifying backs, Tuten is balling, ranking ninth in explosive run rate, eighth in yards after contact per attempt, and sixth in missed tackle rate. Tuten will have tough sledding this week. He'll need a touchdown to pay off likely. Houston's run defense has remained top shelf all season, allowing the fourth-lowest explosive run rate, the fourth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the 11th-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

With David Montgomery sidelined with a groin issue, Wood Marks should be Houston's workhorse back. Last week in the final three quarters of the game, Marks played 95.7% of the snaps, with all 13 of the running back rushing attempts after Montgomery left the game. Marks had a 66.7% route share and 11.5% target share in the final three quarters. Marks has been very efficient with his workload this season. Among 42 qualifying rushers, Marks ranks 12th in explosive run rate and seventh in missed tackle rate. Marks will have to rely upon his volume and touchdown equity in the Houston offense this week because he won't find much running room against one of the best run defenses in the NFL. Jacksonville has allowed the second-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the lowest yards after contact per attempt and missed tackle rate.

Last week. MarShawn Lloyd played 44.1% of the snaps (led the team) among the backs with 38.5% of the rushing share and a 26.5% route share. The blowout nature of that game probably tilts some of the usage stats more in the direction of Pierre Strong. Lloyd also led the team with two red zone rushing attempts (Strong, one). As a rusher, Lloyd has only 1.32 yards after contact per attempt (WOOF), but he has managed a 17% missed tackle rate. Last week, with his two scores, Lloyd was the RB14 for the week while finishing with 11 touches and 37 total yards. Lloyd could have another strong RB2/flex week against Dallas. The Cowboys have allowed the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the 10th-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards before contact per attempt.

Jeremiyah Love remains in a frustrating committee with Tyler Allgeier. It looks like this is partially because of his health, as Love continues to manage/battle through an ankle injury. Over the last two games, Love has averaged 13.5 touches and 38.5 total yards with a 47% snap rate, 59.1% of the rushing attempts, a 19.4% route share, and only a 2.4% target share. Among 42 qualifying backs, Love is 41st in explosive run rate, 25th in yards after contact per attempt, and 21st in missed tackle rate. Love remains a viable flex play this week with a good matchup. The Rams have allowed the highest rushing success rate, the ninth-highest explosive run rate, and the eighth-most yards before contact per attempt. Love opened this week with a DNP.

Since Week 2, Tony Pollard has been the RB29 in fantasy points per game, averaging 17.1 touches and 65.8 total yards. Since Week 2, Pollard has had a 53.1% snap rate, a 64.9% rushing share, and a 29.2% route share (6.5% target share). Among 42 qualifying rushers, Pollard is 24th in explosive run rate and 16th in yards after contact per attempt. Pollard is a decent flex who could be an RB2 this week if he gets into the endzone. Indy has allowed the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the second-most yards before contact per attempt, and the ninth-highest missed tackle rate.

I'm expecting Saquon Barkley to be out again this week. With Barkley sidelined, Dameon Pierce likely operates as Philly's workhorse back. Last week, in the final two quarters of the game without Will Shipley, Pierce played every snap for Philly with every running back rushing attempt and a 64% route share. He finished the game with 13 touches for only 12 yards. Against the Jags' elite run defense and behind his makeshift offensive line, Pierce saw -0.09 yards before contact per attempt while producing 1.36 yards after contact per attempt and a 6% missed tackle rate. He was hit at or behind the line of scrimmage on 72.7% of his rushing attempts. He should find more running room this week against Carolina's struggling run defense. Pierce isn't a sexy play for Week 6, but he could see enough volume in a plus matchup to produce RB2/flex value. Carolina has allowed the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, and the second-most yards after contact per attempt.

Alvin Kamara is banged up. Last week, he had only a 27.9% snap rate with 17.6% of the rushing attempts and a 7.7% route share. I'd love to tell you to flex Kamara this week, but with this minuscule playing time, I can't. Kamara is dealing with a back issue. He opened this week with a limited practice session.

After seeing at least four targets in every game he has been active for this season, last week RJ Harvey goose egged in the passing game with only one target and zero production through the air. For a struggling passing offense, it was head-scratching. Harvey has averaged 8.8 touches and 47 total yards as Denver's passing down back. Harvey has only seen 15.8% of the rushing attempts while logging a 42.6% route share and 17.5% target share. Harvey is back on the PPR flex radar this week against a Seattle pass defense that has allowed the fifth-most receptions to backs and the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game to the position.

The Broncos have been forcing the issue with J.K. Dobbins. Denver has been leaning on him since Week 3, as he has averaged 17 touches and 59.6 total yards, but that doesn't mean it has been a good idea. Since Week 3, Dobbins has had a 45.3% snap rate, 60.5% of the rushing attempts, and a 14.8% route share. Among 42 qualifying backs, Dobbins has been limping along in the efficiency departments, sitting at 31st in explosive run rate and 39th in missed tackle rate. Dobbins remains a touchdown-dependent flex. He's a bust if he doesn't get into the endzone again this week. I don't see him maximizing his touches in this horrible matchup. Seattle has limited rushers to the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, the tenth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the sixth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Bill saw his role diminish with only a 35% snap rate, 36.7% of the rushing attempts, and a 16.2% route share. The route share wasn't a shock, but seeing Rachaad White eat into the early downs is concerning. Jacory Croskey-Merritt finished with 11 rushing attempts, 82 yards on the ground, and a score. Bill hasn't had much room to run this season behind Washington's horrible offensive line. Among 42 qualifying rushers, Bill ranks 37th in explosive run rate, 21st in yards after contact per attempt, 41st in missed tackle rate, and has been hit at or behind the line of scrimmage at the third-highest rate (50.7%). His offensive line has generated only 1.48 yards before contact per attempt, which is being inflated by the Giants' horrible run defense. Last week, Bill had 4.09 yards before contact per attempt. In three of his five games this season, he hasn't had more than 1.11 yards before contact per attempt. Bill is a touchdown-dependent flex this week that likely busts. The 49ers have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the eighth-lowest missed tackle rate.

I can't overstate how much I absolutely hate everything that Mike McDaniel is doing. Last week, Hampton led the team with 41.2% of the rushing share while playing the third-fewest snaps (31.7%) for the backfield. Hampton is being utilized as an early down option only, as he had only two routes last week. Hampton still has a solid 10.8% explosive run rate and 2.45 yards after contact per attempt, but that doesn't seem to matter to the Bolts' offensive coordinator. Sit Hampton in a bad rushing matchup. Kansas City has limited rushers to the eighth-lowest rushing success rate, the fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.
Quinshon Judkins (ankle) didn't practice to open the week. His Week 6 status is up in the air. I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Last week, Kendre Miller took over as New Orleans' primary early down back with 58.8% of the team's rushing attempts while playing 30.2% of the snaps. Miller finished with ten rushing attempts and 30 rushing yards (one score). Miller hasn't had an explosive run this season while logging only 1.45 yards after contact per attempt and a 14% missed tackle rate. None of those metrics are good. Miller is a touchdown-dependent flex play. Miller at least has a good matchup this week. The Giants have allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fourth-highest rushing success rate, and the ninth-highest yards after contact per attempt.

Blake Corum is a nice flex play this week. The betting line is telling all of us that the Rams run away with this game, which could mean more work for Corum. Last week, Corum played 24.4% of the snaps with a 14.5% route share, 21.7% of the rushing attempts, and a 7.4% target share. He finished with eight touches and 72 total yards (one score). Among 42 qualifying rushers, he is sixth in explosive run rate and 17th in missed tackle rate. The Cards have allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the third-highest missed tackle rate. Corum could see 10-12 touches in this game. If he gets into the endzone, he could easily be an RB2 this week, as he was in Week 5 (RB15).

Last week, Rachaad White returned and had a 60% snap rate, a 32.4% route share, a 4% target share, eight touches, and 20 total yards. White is an interesting PPR flex this week. Washington will likely be playing catch-up mode in this game, which could mean a lot of White on the field. White has an 8% target share, a 16% target per route run rate, and 0.85 YPRR this season. The 49ers have quietly allowed the most receptions to running backs and the second-most receiving fantasy points per game to the position.

Over the last two games, Tyler Allgeier has continued to play a prominent role in the Arizona backfield as Jeremiyah Love plays through injury. Allgeier has had a 49.3% snap rate, 25% of the rushing attempts, and a 33.3% route share (4.8% target share). He has averaged 7.5 touches and 32.5 total yards. Allgeier is a deep league flex again this week. Among 42 qualifying rushers, he is sixth in yards after contact per attempt and 37th in missed tackle rate. The Rams have been gashed on the ground. The Rams have allowed the highest rushing success rate, the ninth-highest explosive run rate, and the eighth-most yards before contact per attempt.

Brian Robinson Jr. is the RB21 in fantasy points per game, but one outing in a five-week sample with 11 PPR points and another with 25.2 PPR points can falsely inflate your fantasy stock. Outside of his four touchdowns this season helping his fantasy value, he has averaged 10.8 touches and 46.4 total yards. He has been good on a per-touch basis, though. Among 42 qualifying backs, Robinson is fifth in yards after contact per attempt and 16th in missed tackle rate. Robinson could easily get into the end zone again this week and flirt with RB2 production. Chicago's run defense has stunk, allowing the third-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-lowest stuff rate.
Kyle Monangai opened this week with a DNP (toe/thumb). I'm expecting him to miss this week, but I'll revisit his status on Friday.
Breece Hall opened this week with a DNP (quad). I'm expecting him to miss this week, but I'll update his outlook on Friday.
TreVeyon Henderson sustained an ankle injury last week. He opened this week with a limited practice session. I'm expecting him to miss this week, but I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Last week was the monster performance that everyone had been waiting for with George Pickens. CeeDee Lamb getting banged up and a ton of single-high coverage helped facilitate that, though. Pickens has only one other game this season with more than 11 PPR points. Overall, he has a 20.8% target share with 2.06 YPRR, four red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 24.4% first-read share. The big issue for Pickens this week is that he'll see another secondary that loves to utilize two-high coverage. Green Bay has the fifth-highest rate of two high in the NFL (62.6%). Against two high, Pickens' target per route run rate drops to 15% and his YPRR dips to 1.59. Those aren't great numbers at all. The Packers haven't been a shutdown unit against perimeter wide receivers, so it's possible that Pickens gets a touchdown this week and saves a middling stat line. Green Bay is 16th in yards per target allowed to perimeter wide receivers while also giving up the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity.

Matthew Golden has been absolutely fantastic this season as the WR16 in fantasy points per game. Golden has a 22.7% target share with 2.48 YPRR, eight red zone targets, ten deep targets, and a 26.1% first-read share. He has been crushing. Golden should feast again this week. Over the last two weeks, Dallas has utilized single high at the second-highest rate (68.2%). Against single high, Golden leads the team with a 26% target-per-route run rate with 1.78 YPRR. Dallas has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to wide receivers.

Michael Wilson had a surprising down week in Week 5, but he is still a top-24 fantasy wide receiver (WR24 in fantasy points per game). Wilson has a 24% target share with 1.47 YPRR, eight red zone targets, a 29.9% first-read share, and seven deep targets. Wilson should see a boatload of volume again this week, but I'm not expecting a ton of efficiency. The Rams have held perimeter wide receivers to the sixth-fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per game. It's also possible that Trent McDuffie follows Wilson this week. McDuffie followed Malik Nabers and Dontayvion Wicks on 51.6-75% of their routes, holding them to a combined four targets and seven receiving yards in his coverage.

Tetairoa McMillan is the WR10 in fantasy points per game with a 22.7% target share, 2.41 YPRR, a 31.6% first-read share, five red zone targets, and six deep targets. McMillan has been fantastic. Bryce Young will continue to lean on him this week, so the target volume should be there. The matchup is quite tough, so don't expect a ceiling performance from McMillan, though. Philly has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Jalen Coker opened this week with a full practice (estimated). I expect him to be back this week, but we have to see what his practice participation looks like this week. I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Denzel Boston is the WR22 in fantasy points per game. Among 111 qualifying receivers, Boston ranks 36th in target share (18.2%), 31st in YPRR (2.10), and 46th in first-read share (21.2%). Boston has four red zone targets and a whopping nine deep targets. This week, Boston faces a Baltimore secondary that has utilized two high at the fourth-highest rate (63.9%). Well, last week was frustrating. With Mack Holins out and a perfect schematic matchup for Doubs, I expected him to crush. Then I got to see Drake Maye light up the Raiders' secondary and Doubs lose his invitation to the passing attack party. Last week, Doubs led the team with a 94.2% route share, but he had only an 8.8% target share and 12.5% first-read share. UGH! Freiermuth will need a touchdown to likely save his fantasy day this week because I'm not projecting an encore of last week's game in Week 6.

His production has taken a hit since suffering an ankle injury in Week 4, but looks to have turned a corner as the Seahawks did not list him with an injury status for Thursday Night Footall. Fire Williams up as DT1/DL2 option despite the tough on paper matchup.

Nik Bonitto was at it again in Week 5, tallying three solos, one assist, two sacks, and three tackles for loss. Bonitto is up to three sacks on the season, with all three coming in his last three games. Bonitto is one of the best in the league when he is on, and his recent production suggests that he is ready to roll. Tap him as a top-10 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Elijah Ponder was at it again in Week 5, racking up four solos, two assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Ponder is up to a new career high of 4.5 sacks and should have at least a few more weeks of starter-level snaps while Harold Landry remains on the mend. Ponder has a tasty matchup in Week 5 against the New York Jets, making him a DL2 option. Tap Ponder as a top-25 option as long as he is cooking.

Byron Murphy was at it again in Week 5, racking up five solos, one assist, two sacks, and three tackles for loss. Murphy is up to three sacks on the season, with all three coming in his last two games. His hot streak puts him in the DT1 mix for the byes and makes him a deep league DL3 option during the byes. However, Murphy should remain on fantasy benches for Thursday Night Football. Look elsewhere for Week 6.

Akheem Mesidor stepped up in Week 5, tallying five solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Mesidor is up to 2.5 sacks on the season, with a sack in two of his last three games. Akheem has looked the part through the first five weeks of the season and may be set to see an expanded role in the near future with Khalil Mack emerging as one of the hottest trade candidates in the league. Mesidor should be rostered in all leagues as a bye week depth piece who could emerge as a DL2/3 option in the next couple of weeks.

Princely Umanmielen was at it again in Week 4, racking up three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss on a season high 52 percent of the snaps. Princely has been a force off the edge for the Panthers, recording a sack in three of his first four contests of the season. He could see an expanded role in Week 6 if Jaelan Phillips sees his snaps scaled back in an effort to prevent further injury. If Jaelan Phillips misses Week 6, Umanmielen becomes a must-start DL3 with DL2 upside.

Keion White was excellent in Week 5, racking up three solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Keion is now up to three sacks on the season and has recorded at least one sack in three of his last four games. White has seen an expanded role over the last two weeks due to Nick Bosa being sidelined with a quad injury and has produced well enough to factor prominently in the rotation until he cools down.

D.J. Jones showed up in Week 5, tallying one solo, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 46 percent of the snaps. The sack was the first of the season for Jones, who is part of a deep rotation along the Broncos' defensive interior. Keep him in mind for 32-team leagues but look elsewhere for Week 6 in all other formats.

Ernest Jones was at it again in Week 5, posting five solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Jones has ridden one splash week and two spike weeks to LB2 status through five weeks of action and deserves to be treated as an elite top-five option while he is cooking.

Alex Singleton stayed hot in Week 5, notching five solos, two assists, and one tackle for loss. Singleton has four spike weeks to his name, cementing him as an LB1 play going forward. The LB14 through five weeks of action, tap Singleton as a top-12 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Frankie Luvu showed up in Week 5, tallying six solos and three assists. Luvu was injured in Week 1, causing him to miss two weeks of action. Luvu has proven LB2 upside, but based on last season and a potentially injury-fueled slow start to the season, it is better to view him as an LB3 play until he proves otherwise. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 6 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football.

Jake Hansen showed up in Week 5, reeling off three solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, one interception, and two passes defended. Hansen had a splash week in Week 4, and now with a spike week in Week 5, Hansen has forced his way into must-start LB3 territory. His upside has been plain for all to see, making Hansen an ideal plug-and-play option until Henry To'oTo'o returns.

Dee Winters showed up in Week 5, racking up six solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Winters has proven to be a solid LB3 play so far, with two games with six or more solos and four games with four or more. There was an expectation that Winters would see an everydown role for Dallas, but his issues in coverage and lack of playcalling/green dot acumen have kept him closer to the 70 percent range most weeks, effectively capping his upside and dropping his floor; hence the LB3 tag. Tap Winters as a top-36 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Pete Werner stepped up in Week 5, notching four solos and six assists on 100 percent of the snaps. Werner has seen an expanded role over the last two weeks due to Kaden Elliss dealing with a calf injury. Werner was trending as an LB3 prior to Elliss being sidelined, but should now be considered part of the top-25 conversation for as long as Kaden is sidelined. Werner has one splash week and two near spike weeks to his name and has managed to stay fantasy relevant despite splitting time with Danny Stutsman. Start Werner as an LB2 while Elliss is out and an LB3 when he returns.

Trenton Simpson stayed hot in Week 5, racking up five solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss under the bright lights of Sunday Night Football. Simpson has now recorded a spike week in three straight games and is still hovering around the 55-60 snap share mark despite Teddye Buchanan seeing his own snaps expanded. This suggests that Simpson is locked into his role until further notice, which should be all the impetus fantasy managers need to make him a priority add this week. The LB12 through five weeks of action, the Ravens linebacker should be rostered in all competitive leagues; act accordingly.

Justin Strnad showed up in Week 5, racking up five solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. It was the first spike week of the season for Strnad, who saw a season high in snaps with both Pat Surtain and Riley Moss ruled out. Strnad becomes an option when four teams are on bye, so tap him as an LB4/flex2 option where needed for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football.

Arguably the most exciting safety in the league not named Kyle Hamilton, Nick Emmanwori has taken some time to round back into health but showed up in Week 4 and had a solid Week 5 that saw him record three solos, one assist, and one pressure.

Brandon Jones stepped up in Week 5, racking up two solos, two assists, one fumble recovery, one interception, and one pass defended. Jones has one splash week and two spike weeks in his last three games, a stretch that has pushed him up to DB4 overall on the season. Suffice it to say that Jones needs to be started everywhere as a top-15 option for Thursday Night Football.

Witherspoon should be counted as a top-three CB option, who doubles as a DB2 play for Thursday Night Football. The rare corner you start every week, even in DB leagues, Devon should be started in all formats for the plus Week 6 battle.

Amik Robertson was excellent in Week 5, tallying six solos, one assist, and one pass defended. Amik has been cooking for IDP managers with three straight spike weeks and narrowly missing a fourth. The corner has registered four or more solos in four straight contests and is currently the DB6/CB1 in total fantasy points at the position. Suffice it to say that Robertson should be rostered absolutely everywhere as a DB3 option for Week 6 and beyond.

Ji'Ayir Brown stepped up in Week 5, racking up six solos, one assist, and one pass defended. Brown now has two spike weeks to his name and becomes a low-end DB3 option during the byes. His floor remains DB5/bench level, as he has mustered just two games with four or more solos. He does possess DB3 upside, but is likely not someone you should be planning on utilizing when the bye weeks wrap up unless he starts to show more consistency.

Jacob Parrish was at it again in Week 5, posting eight solos, one assist, and four passes defended. Parrish has recorded back-to-back spike weeks and has tallied four or more solos in three straight contests. The DB29 in total fantasy points through five weeks of play, Parrish is a CB1/DB3 option, especially during the byes.

Jeremy Reaves stepped up for IDP managers in Week 5, recording four solos, three assists, and one pass defended. Reaves has no spike weeks to his name thus far but has managed to post four or more solos in four straight games. Reaves is a solid DB3/4 bye week filler type during the byes and should be rostered in competitive leagues with larger benches.

Quinyon Mitchell stayed hot in Week 5, reeling off four solos, one assist, one interception, and two passes defended. Quinyon has posted two spike weeks in his last three games (he was injured in the other) and has registered four or more solos in four straight contests. The DB24 through five weeks of action, Mitchell should be rostered in all competitive leagues as a DB3 with DB2 upside. Start him with confidence for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.
